title: Career roadmap · Aviation Policy Researcher
summary: Build from aviation research into regulation, economics, policy evaluation, stakeholder analysis and evidence-based recommendations for governments, regulators, airports and international aviation organisations.

facts.Timeline assumption: Because the selected qualification is a Ph.D., 2026 is treated as Ph.D. Year 1. The roadmap prioritises research output, policy-writing ability, quantitative analysis, aviation regulation and direct exposure to government/industry policy work.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build expertise in aviation regulation, economics, policy research and quantitative methods; publish policy-relevant research.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Become a specialist in one policy domain: airport policy, airline regulation, safety, sustainability, competition, connectivity or emerging aviation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead policy studies and advise government, regulators, airports, airlines or international organisations.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become a senior aviation-policy strategist able to evaluate AI, drones, advanced air mobility, climate policy and changing global aviation rules.

2040–2046: Senior Aviation Policy Adviser → Director of Aviation Policy / International Aviation Policy Specialist

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

The strongest policy researcher will be more than an aviation subject-matter expert. Build the ability to interpret regulation, quantify economic effects, evaluate competing policy options and communicate recommendations to decision-makers. Maintain international awareness because aviation policy increasingly crosses national borders, particularly for emissions, safety standards, market access, digital systems, drones and advanced air mobility.
